items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: On blues, except you played a mighty good beat, slow blues, because most of the time, Jooks, Balleisers, people danced, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah. Um, can you tell me something about the style of blues up here in Chicago? They began calling it Boogie Woogie piano, like Pinetop and all those numbers. And the Pinetop's Boogie Woogie. Did they ever play that style based down south?

Well, that's practically all we played. You'd have to play that style for people to dance by. On blues, except you played a mighty good beat, slow blues, because most of the time, Jooks, Balleisers, people danced, you know. Yeah. Well, that's mostly we played, but we didn't call it Pinetop's Boogie Woogie. We didn't call it Boogie Woogie at all. They called it Dudlow Joe.
Dudlow Joe. Dudlow Joe. That was the style of the bass, you mean, isn't it? That's right. Rolling bass and different types. Oh, Cal Cal Davenport, when did you first hear him or meet him?
